text: dsh-stream-timeout-fix 是 DSH 主机插件，为 Node fetch 全局 undici dispatcher 设置更长的流静默和响应头超时，减少 LLM SSE 长暂停时因默认 300 秒限制而中断。默认 body 超时 30 分钟、headers 超时 10 分钟，可用环境变量或插件选项调整。适合使用第三方或自托管 OpenAI 兼容端点的 DSH 部署；不提供重试或模型服务配置。需要 Node.js 22.19 以上及 undici。

dsh-stream-timeout-fix extends Node fetch's undici timeouts so silent LLM streams avoid the default 300-second cutoff. Body timeout defaults to 30 minutes, headers to 10; both are configurable. For DSH users of self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Requires Node.js 22.19+ and undici.
DSH 的模型流停顿几分钟后就断开，有办法延长等待吗？
想让长时间没有新 token 的 SSE 回复继续等下去。

能不能调高 Node fetch 等待流数据的超时时间？
希望请求头或首个响应字节较慢时别太早失败。
怎样避免长时间静默的模型输出被客户端当成网络中断？
How can I keep a silent LLM stream from timing out after five minutes?
I need longer header and body timeouts for Node fetch in my DSH host.
dsh-stream-timeout-fix 的功能「延长流静默超时」：为全局 undici Agent 设置 bodyTimeout，允许 LLM SSE 流在较长字节间隔后继续。插件挂载时自动生效，默认值为 30 分钟。
dsh-stream-timeout-fix 的功能「延长响应头等待」：调高 Agent 的 headersTimeout，让请求有更长时间等待响应首字节；挂载后作用于全局 dispatcher，默认 10 分钟。
dsh-stream-timeout-fix 的功能「调整超时配置」：可用 DSH_STREAM_TIMEOUT_BODY_MS、DSH_STREAM_TIMEOUT_HEADERS_MS 环境变量或插件选项设置两个超时，非负数选项优先。
dsh-stream-timeout-fix 的功能「重复挂载保护」：apply 检查进程中的运行标记，若已有 Agent 就记录提示并跳过，避免再次替换全局 dispatcher。

A tiny **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)** host plugin that stops Node's built-in `fetch`
from killing long, silently-stalled LLM streams — the ones that die with

```
TypeError: terminated        (cause: BodyTimeoutError, UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT)
```

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · dsh-stream-timeout-fix：after roughly 304–305 seconds of mid-stream silence, and get reported as a
`TRANSPORT` failure even though the provider never hung up.

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · dsh-stream-timeout-fix：> **Who this is for.** Third-party / self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints whose
> responses can take a long time and occasionally stall mid-stream: university or
> company private deployments, LiteLLM-style gateways, self-hosted vLLM, and the
> like. Against a well-behaved large cloud API you probably do not need it.
>
> **Maintenance.** Written by the author for personal use, and published in case it
> helps someone else. It may not be actively maintained, issues and PRs may go
> unanswered, and there is no support commitment. The plugin is ~120 lines — read it
> before you install it. See **Validation status** below: the fix is confirmed by a real
> 607 s silence that survived end-to-end.
>
> **Distribution.** There is no npm package — this is a small single-purpose patch and
> does not warrant one. Install straight from this repository; see [Install](#install).

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · The symptom：With a streaming LLM endpoint, some requests fail like this:

* the SSE response is **already established and content has started flowing**
  (reasoning tokens, partial answers, tool-call deltas), then
* **nothing arrives for minutes** while the upstream keeps generating, and then
* the request dies locally after ~304–305 s of silence with
  `TypeError: terminated`, classified as a transport/network error.

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · The symptom：The provider's own logs show the opposite of a provider-side failure: it records a
**client disconnect** (LiteLLM / nginx log `499`) and the upstream **still finishes
generating and still bills the tokens** — you pay for output you never received.

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · The root cause：Node's built-in `fetch` runs on [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici), which
ships two client-side clocks that are invisible until they fire:

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · The root cause：| Clock | Default | Applies to | Error when it fires |
|---|---|---|---|
| `headersTimeout` | `300_000 ms` | waiting for the first response byte | `TypeError: fetch failed`, cause `HeadersTimeoutError` (`UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT`) |
| `bodyTimeout` | `300_000 ms` | idle gap **between body bytes** (re-armed by every received byte) | `TypeError: terminated`, cause `BodyTimeoutError` (`UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT`) |

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · The root cause：Because `bodyTimeout` is re-armed per byte, ordinary slow-but-flowing streams are
never affected (streams running 20+ minutes are fine). It only bites when the
**gap** exceeds 300 s — exactly what a stalled upstream produces.

Two things make this hard to attribute correctly:

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · The root cause：1. `bodyTimeout` reports itself as **`terminated`**, i.e. literally "the other side
   disconnected". Nothing points at the client's own clock.
2. DSH's failure classifier matches `/terminated/` and maps it to `TRANSPORT`
   (see `dsh-llm-pi-ai`), which reads as a network/provider problem.

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · The root cause：So the observable facts (client disconnect in the provider log, `499`, successful
upstream generation, a `TRANSPORT` error on our side) all look like "the platform
drops idle connections at ~300 s" — while the actual killer is our own default.

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · What this plugin does：DSH's LLM path never passes a custom `fetch`
(`dsh-llm-pi-ai` → `pi-ai` → OpenAI SDK v6 → `globalThis.fetch` → **global undici
dispatcher**), so one process-wide swap covers every provider at once:

```js
setGlobalDispatcher(new Agent({ bodyTimeout: 1_800_000, headersTimeout: 600_000 }))
```

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · What this plugin does：* `bodyTimeout = 30 min`, `headersTimeout = 10 min` by default — finite on purpose,
  so a genuinely dead peer is still reclaimed.
* Stream-level watchdogs (e.g. pi-ai's `streamIdleTimeoutMs`) and provider retry
  policies remain the real guards; this plugin only removes the *disagreement*
  between two idle clocks.
* Cross-version injection is fine: the global dispatcher lives in a process-wide
  `Symbol.for('undici.globalDispatcher.1')` slot, so an `Agent` created by undici
  8.x is honored by Node's built-in `fetch` (undici 7.x).

end-to-end. In order of evidential strength:

  started flowing, never in the headers phase.
* **Field data, 2026-10-13 → 2026-10-28.** Across the recorded failures since
  installation (structural count from `stream finish` events, not log text), the
  targeted class — `TRANSPOR

If a request still dies during a long silence, compare the gap length and the message:
**304–305 s** points at an undici default clock somewhere in the stack; **exactly 300 s**
with `pi-ai stream idle timeout` points at DSH's own watchdog; **`Request timed out.`**
points at the SDK's `timeoutMs` (headers phase); anything else points at a
server/gateway idle limit — which this plugin does not address.

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · Install：**Requires Node ≥ 22.19** — that is the `undici` dependency's engine requirement
(`engines.node >= 22.19.0`). Any DSH build able to mount this plugin already bundles
undici 8.x itself, so this matches the real deployment range; on Node 20 the import
fails instead of silently misbehaving.

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · Install from this repository：```bash
git clone https://github.com/SundaeYAGO/dsh-stream-timeout-fix
cd dsh-stream-timeout-fix
npm install     # fetches the `undici` dependency the plugin imports
```

Then mount the checkout as a local bundle in your profile:

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · Install from this repository：The package's own `cordis.patch.yml` mounts the plugin row, so no manual profile-patch
edit is needed. If your DSH CLI accepts git specs (the same form other DSH plugins use),
`dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:SundaeYAGO/dsh-stream-timeout-fix` should
perform those three steps for you.

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · Verify：* The loader lists the entry as enabled/active (`include:stream-timeout-fix`).
* The host log contains one activation line:
  `[stream-timeout-fix] global dispatcher replaced: bodyTimeout=1800000ms, headersTimeout=600000ms ...`
* Runtime marker: `globalThis.__streamTimeoutFix` holds the installed `Agent`,
  the effective timeouts, and the runtime versions.
* The real proof is passive: the next 300+ s stall your provider has will no longer
  kill the request. If a request *does* still die during a long silence, check the
  gap length — anything clearly different from 304–305 s points at a genuine
  server/gateway idle limit rather than this client clock.

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · Configuration：| Setting | Default | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `bodyTimeoutMs` | `1800000` | patch row `config`, or env `DSH_STREAM_TIMEOUT_BODY_MS` |
| `headersTimeoutMs` | `600000` | patch row `config`, or env `DSH_STREAM_TIMEOUT_HEADERS_MS` |

Set either to `0` to disable that clock entirely (not recommended globally — you
lose the last-resort reclamation of dead sockets).

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · What this plugin does not do：* **No retries.** It ships no retry policy and never re-sends a request. Retrying is
  the job of DSH's own retry plugin (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-retry`), configured per
  provider in your profile patch — see the pairing section below if you want both.
* **No provider, auth or routing configuration.** It mounts no service, registers no
  tool, and touches no endpoint or credential.
* **No cost control.** It cannot cap, cancel or budget anything — read the next section.
* **No server-side change.** If your gateway has its own idle-connection limit, this
  plugin will not help; ask your operator for SSE comment heartbeats instead.
* **No change to DSH's own stream watchdog.** `streamIdleTimeoutMs` is per-route
  configuration (`dsh-llm-pi-ai`), not something a dispatcher swap can touch — see
  “Raise `streamIdleTimeoutMs` as well”.

cuts a silent stream at `streamIdleTimeoutMs` (default `300000`), reporting
`pi-ai stream idle timeout after 300000ms` with `code: TIMEOUT`.

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · Raise `streamIdleTimeoutMs` as well (needed for >300 s silences)：That is not theory: on 2026-10-18 two attempts died at exactly **300.02 s** and
**300.04 s** with this plugin active (undici ceiling already 30 min), because
`streamIdleTimeoutMs` was unset on the route. Without raising it, the plugin improves
the *diagnosis* (honest `TIMEOUT` instead of `TRANSPORT`) but does **not** extend how
long a silence can last.

```yaml

    streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1800000   # 30 min — must exceed the longest stall you want to survive

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · The four clocks that can cut a stream：| # | Clock | Owner | Where it bites | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `headersTimeout` | undici (this plugin) | no response headers yet | 300 s → **600 s** here |
| 2 | `bodyTimeout` | undici (this plugin) | silence between chunks | 300 s → **1800 s** here |
| 3 | `streamIdleTimeoutMs` | `dsh-llm-pi-ai` | silence, first byte included | 300 000 ms |
| 4 | `timeoutMs` | `dsh-llm-pi-ai` → openai SDK | **headers phase** (`Request timed out.`, code `TIMEOUT`) | SDK default **600 000 ms** |

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · The four clocks that can cut a stream：Clock 4 is the sneaky one: it is the OpenAI SDK's request timeout and it surfaces as
`Request timed out.` / `TIMEOUT` — easy to mistake for a platform failure. Set both on
the route:

```yaml

    streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1800000   # clock 3 — idle gaps, first byte included
    timeoutMs: 1800000             # clock 4 — headers phase (SDK request timeout)

text:
dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · Cost and billing (please read)：The plugin makes **no network requests of its own** and adds no cost by itself. But it
changes the *outcome* of a stall, and that has a price:

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · Cost and billing (please read)：* Before: the request was killed at ~304 s, and you paid for tokens you never received.
* After: the request keeps waiting while the provider keeps generating — and the
  provider bills those tokens. You now pay for output you actually receive, and the
  request may take minutes longer.
* Combined with an unlimited retry policy, repeated stalls can multiply token spend
  (most providers bill every failed attempt too). Budget accordingly, watch your usage
  dashboard, and prefer smaller outputs.
* The clocks are finite on purpose (30 min / 10 min): a genuinely dead peer is still
  reclaimed instead of hanging forever.

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · Pairing with a retry policy (optional, not shipped)：Automatic retries belong to your profile patch
(`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`), not to this plugin. Example for a
provider route:

```yaml
providers:
  your-provider:
    retryPolicy:
      mode: always              # no retry cap; ignores retryableCodes

Choose delays that respect your provider's rate limit (institutional deployments often
have a small per-key RPM), and keep the cost note above in mind: **retries are billed**.

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · Scope and caveats：* **Process-wide by design.** Every `fetch` in the DSH host process (all
  providers, other plugins) loses the 300 s default ceiling and inherits the
  configured one. That is the point, but it is a real blast radius.
* **Cross-version dispatcher reports are tested, not assumed.** Several upstream
  discussions (`#7721`, `#7671`, `#7598`, `#7468`, `#7502`) blame a *userland*
  undici 8.x dispatcher in the process-global slot for breaking content-encoding and
  response headers on Node's built-in fetch (bundled undici 7.x) — the same slot
  this plugin swaps. `scripts/check-content-encoding.mjs` (part of `npm test`)
  verifies gzip decoding **before and after** the swap; it passes on Node 24.21 with
  undici 8.11.2. If you ever see raw gzip/brotli or missing headers after
  installing, disable the plugin and report your `node -v` plus
  `process.versions.undici` pair.
* **Not a cure for upstream stalls.** If your provider pauses for minutes, the
  request still takes minutes. Pair this with a retry policy, and prefer smaller
  outputs so a stall costs less.
* **Client-side keepalive is not an option.** After an HTTP/1.1 POST body is

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · How it was diagnosed：1. A non-streaming probe died at **t = 304.6 s** with `HeadersTimeoutError` —
   an **undici exception class**, which revealed the client-side clocks.
2. Every production failure was re-checked: silence gaps of **304.6–305.4 s**,
   `message: "terminated"`, always mid-stream, always after content started.
3. A local controlled reproduction (local SSE server, real Node fetch) reproduced
   the fingerprint exactly: last byte at `t = 2.045 s` → error at `t = 306.062 s`
   (`TypeError: terminated`, cause `BodyTimeoutError`, code `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT`),
   while a client built with `Agent({ bodyTimeout: 0 })` survived **338 s** of
   silence and completed the stream. `setGlobalDispatcher` from a differently
   versioned undici copy also fixed the built-in `fetch` — the injection path this
   plugin uses.

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · How it was diagnosed：`scripts/reproduce-300s.mjs` ships that reproduction:

```bash
node scripts/reproduce-300s.mjs            # default fetch: reproduces the ~304 s kill
node scripts/reproduce-300s.mjs --plugin   # after this plugin: survives past 300 s
```

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · Development：```bash
npm install
npm test
```

`npm test` runs a fast, deterministic pair:

* **control** — an `Agent` with a tiny `bodyTimeout` proves that a silent stream
  dies with `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT` (the reported failure shape);
* **fix** — after `apply()`, the same silence completes, and the global dispatcher
  is verified to be this plugin's agent;
* plus header-phase survival and idempotent re-mount checks.

一个极小的 **DeepSeek Harness（DSH）** 宿主侧插件：阻止 Node 内置 `fetch` 掐死
「长时间静默的 LLM 流」——那些在流中途静默约 **304–305 秒**后死于

```
TypeError: terminated        (cause: BodyTimeoutError, UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT)
```

并被归类为 `TRANSPORT` 失败的请求。**而平台侧其实从未挂断我们。**

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · dsh-stream-timeout-fix：> **适用场景**：面向「响应时间长、且偶尔在流中途停顿」的**第三方 / 自建
> OpenAI 兼容端点**——例如学校、公司的私有化部署，LiteLLM 之类的网关，
> 自托管 vLLM 等。如果你用的是行为良好的大型云 API，大概不需要它。
>
> **维护声明**：作者出于**自用目的**编写，顺手开源给可能遇到同样问题的人。
> **不保证持续维护**——issue / PR 可能不会及时处理，也没有任何支持承诺。
> 插件本体约 120 行，安装前请自行过一遍代码。下文「验证状态」里已有**实测确认**：
> 一次持续 **607 秒**的静默被成功挺过。
>
> **分发方式**：**不发 npm 包**——这只是一个小补丁，不值得单独发个包。

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 现象：流式 LLM 端点偶尔这样失败：

* SSE 响应**已经建立、内容已经开始吐**（推理 token、部分答案、工具调用增量），然后
* **几分钟没有任何字节**（上游仍在生成），接着
* 本地在静默约 304–305 秒后报 `TypeError: terminated`，被当成传输/网络错误。

而平台侧日志显示的恰好相反：它记录的是**客户端主动断开**（LiteLLM / nginx 记 `499`），
上游**继续生成完并照常计费**——你为压根没收到的那部分 token 付了钱。

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 根因：Node 内置 `fetch` 跑在 [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici) 上，它自带两个**不触发
就完全看不见**的客户端时钟：

| 时钟 | 默认值 | 作用范围 | 触发时的报错 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `headersTimeout` | `300_000 ms` | 等响应第一个字节 | `TypeError: fetch failed`，cause `HeadersTimeoutError`（`UND_ERR_HEADERS_TIMEOUT`） |
| `bodyTimeout` | `300_000 ms` | 响应体**相邻字节之间**的空闲（每收到一个字节重新计时） | `TypeError: terminated`，cause `BodyTimeoutError`（`UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT`） |

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 根因：因为 `bodyTimeout` 按字节重新武装，正常「慢但在流」的请求永远不受影响（跑 20 分钟也没事）；
它只在**静默间隔**超过 300 秒时动手——正是上游 stall 的样子。

两点让它极难被正确归因：

1. `bodyTimeout` 把自己报成 **`terminated`**，字面意思就是「对端断开了」，
   没有任何线索指向客户端自己的时钟；
2. DSH 的失败分类器匹配 `/terminated/` 并归类为 `TRANSPORT`（见 `dsh-llm-pi-ai`），
   读起来就像网络/供应商问题。

于是所有可观察事实（平台日志里的客户端断开、`499`、上游生成成功、我们这侧的
`TRANSPORT`）都指向「平台在 ~300 秒处掐空闲连接」——而真凶是我们自己的默认值。

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 这个插件做什么：DSH 的 LLM 调用链从不传自定义 `fetch`
（`dsh-llm-pi-ai` → `pi-ai` → OpenAI SDK v6 → `globalThis.fetch` → **全局 undici
dispatcher**），所以一次进程级替换就能覆盖所有 provider：

```js
setGlobalDispatcher(new Agent({ bodyTimeout: 1_800_000, headersTimeout: 600_000 }))
```

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 这个插件做什么：* 默认 `bodyTimeout = 30 分钟`、`headersTimeout = 10 分钟`——**故意取有限值**，
  真死的连接终究会被回收。
* 流层看门狗（如 pi-ai 的 `streamIdleTimeoutMs`）与供应商重试策略仍是真正的兜底；
  本插件只是消除**两个空闲时钟之间的口径分歧**。
* 跨版本注入没问题：全局 dispatcher 存在进程级的
  `Symbol.for('undici.globalDispatcher.1')` 槽里，所以 undici 8.x 创建的 `Agent`
  会被 Node 内置 `fetch`（undici 7.x）认账。

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 安装：**要求 Node ≥ 22.19**——这是 `undici` 依赖的 engines 约束（`engines.node >= 22.19.0`）。
任何能挂载本插件的 DSH 版本本身就内置了 undici 8.x，因此这与真实部署范围一致；
在 Node 20 上导入会直接失败，而不是悄悄行为异常。

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 从本仓库安装：```bash
git clone https://github.com/SundaeYAGO/dsh-stream-timeout-fix
cd dsh-stream-timeout-fix
npm install     # 装上插件 import 的 undici 依赖
```

然后把这份 checkout 作为本地 bundle 挂进 profile：

1. 在 `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json` 的 `dependencies` 里加
   `"dsh-stream-timeout-fix": "link:<checkout 的绝对路径>"`；
2. 把 `"dsh-stream-timeout-fix"` 追加进 `dsh.profile.bundles`；
3. 在 profile 目录执行安装/链接（`pnpm install`，它会建好 `node_modules` 链接），
   然后重启 DSH（支持 live bundle 应用的版本会直接热挂载，无需重启）。

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 从本仓库安装：插件自带的 `cordis.patch.yml` 会负责挂载插件行，**无需手改 profile patch**。
如果你的 DSH CLI 接受 git 规格（其它 DSH 插件用的也是这种写法），
`dsh plugin --profile <profile> add github:SundaeYAGO/dsh-stream-timeout-fix`
可以替你完成上面三步。

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 验证：* loader 里该条目为 enabled/active（`include:stream-timeout-fix`）；
* 宿主日志出现一行激活记录：
  `[stream-timeout-fix] global dispatcher replaced: bodyTimeout=1800000ms, headersTimeout=600000ms ...`
* 运行时标记：`globalThis.__streamTimeoutFix` 保存着装上的 `Agent`、生效超时与运行时版本；
* 真正的证明是被动的：下次供应商出现 300+ 秒 stall 时，请求不再被掐死。
  如果某个请求在长静默中**仍然**失败，看间隔长度——明显偏离 304–305 秒的，
  才是平台/网关自己的空闲上限，而不是这个客户端时钟。

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 配置：| 配置项 | 默认 | 位置 |
|---|---|---|
| `bodyTimeoutMs` | `1800000` | patch 行 `config`，或环境变量 `DSH_STREAM_TIMEOUT_BODY_MS` |
| `headersTimeoutMs` | `600000` | patch 行 `config`，或环境变量 `DSH_STREAM_TIMEOUT_HEADERS_MS` |

设为 `0` 表示彻底关闭该时钟（不建议全局这么做——你会失去回收死 socket 的最后手段）。

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 本插件不做什么：* **不含重试**。它不携带任何重试策略，也从不重发请求。重试属于 DSH 自带的重试插件
  （`@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm-retry`），在 profile patch 里按 provider 配置——想两者都用，
  见下面的搭配示例。
* **不碰 provider / 鉴权 / 路由**：不挂载服务、不注册工具、不接触任何端点或密钥。
* **不做费用控制**：它无法限额、取消或预算——请看下一节。
* **不改服务端**：如果你的网关自己有「空闲即断」的限制，本插件帮不上；
  该向运维方要的是服务端 SSE 注释心跳。
* **不改 DSH 自己的流看门狗**：`streamIdleTimeoutMs` 是「按路由」的配置
  （`dsh-llm-pi-ai`），换 dispatcher 动不了它——见下一节。

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 同时调大 `streamIdleTimeoutMs`（要挺过 300+ 秒静默就必须做）：本插件只摘掉 **undici 的** 300 秒时钟。DSH 自己按路由的看门狗仍会在
`streamIdleTimeoutMs`（默认 `300000`）处切断静默流，报
`pi-ai stream idle timeout after 300000ms`（`code: TIMEOUT`）。

这不是理论：2026-10-18 有两次尝试分别死在 **300.02 秒**与 **300.04 秒**，
而当时本插件已生效（undici 上限已是 30 分钟）——因为那条路由没有设
`streamIdleTimeoutMs`。不调大它，本插件只改善**诊断**（诚实的 `TIMEOUT`
取代误导性的 `TRANSPORT`），并**不会**延长可容忍的静默时长。

```yaml
providers:
  your-provider:
    streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1800000   # 30 分钟——必须大于你想挺过的最长 stall
```

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 能切断一条流的四层钟：本插件只管前两层。后两层在 `dsh-llm-pi-ai` 里，**同样值得配置**——2026-10-28
真正切断那条请求的就是第 4 层：

| # | 时钟 | 归属 | 作用阶段 | 默认值 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `headersTimeout` | undici（本插件） | 等响应头 | 300 s → 本插件 **600 s** |
| 2 | `bodyTimeout` | undici（本插件） | 分片之间的静默 | 300 s → 本插件 **1800 s** |
| 3 | `streamIdleTimeoutMs` | `dsh-llm-pi-ai` | 静默（含首字之前） | 300 000 ms |
| 4 | `timeoutMs` | `dsh-llm-pi-ai` → openai SDK | **等响应头**（`Request timed out.`，code `TIMEOUT`） | SDK 默认 **600 000 ms** |
section: 能切断一条流的四层钟

text:
dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 能切断一条流的四层钟：第 4 层最阴险：它是 OpenAI SDK 的请求超时，报错文本是 `Request timed out.` /
`TIMEOUT`，极易被误判成平台故障。建议两层一起显式设：

```yaml
providers:
  your-provider:
    streamIdleTimeoutMs: 1800000   # 第 3 层——静默间隔，含首字之前
    timeoutMs: 1800000             # 第 4 层——响应头阶段（SDK 请求超时）

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 费用与计费（请务必阅读）：插件本身**不发任何网络请求**，自身不产生费用。但它改变了 stall 的**结果**，
而这是有代价的：

* 修复前：请求在 ~304 秒被杀，你**为压根没收到的 token 付了钱**。
* 修复后：请求会继续等待，而 provider 仍在生成——这些 token 同样会计费。
  你现在为**真正收到**的输出付费，但单次请求可能多花几分钟。
* 若再配上「无限重试」策略，反复 stall 会成倍放大 token 支出
  （多数 provider 对每次失败的尝试也计费）。请据此安排预算、盯住用量面板，
  并尽量缩小单次产出规模。
* 默认时钟是**有限值**（30 分钟 / 10 分钟）而非无限：真死的对端仍会被回收，
  不会永久挂起。

text:
dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 影响面与注意事项：* **按设计是进程级的**：宿主进程里所有 `fetch`（全部 provider、其他插件）都不再受
  300 秒默认上限约束，改用你配置的值。这正是目的，但影响面确实存在。
* **跨版本 dispatcher 的已知报告，我们实测而不是想当然**：上游有多条讨论
  （`#7721`、`#7671`、`#7598`、`#7468`、`#7502`）把「userland undici 8.x 的 dispatcher
  装进进程全局槽位」归咎为 Node 内置 fetch（内置 undici 7.x）丢失 content-encoding
  解压与响应头的原因——那正是本插件动的同一个槽位。`scripts/check-content-encoding.mjs`
  （已并入 `npm test`）在**换 dispatcher 前后**各验一次 gzip 解码；在 Node 24.21 +
  undici 8.11.2 上通过。若安装后真的遇到裸 gzip/brotli 或响应头异常，请先停用本插件，
  并附上 `node -v` 与 `process.versions.undici` 一起反馈。
* **治不了上游 stall**：供应商若停顿数分钟，请求就得等数分钟。请配合重试策略，
  并尽量让单次产出小一些，降低 stall 的代价。
* **客户端保活不存在**：HTTP/1.1 下 POST 请求体发完后，客户端在该请求上没有任何
  合法写入位置，且 SSE 是单向的（服务器 → 客户端）。TCP keepalive 与 HTTP/2 PING
  只对「传输层空闲」的中间设备有意义。唯一合法的流内心跳是**服务端发的 SSE 注释**
  （`: ping`）——那是服务端措施。本插件是客户端侧的修法。
* 仅适用于 Node。对 Python/Go/Rust 客户端无效——它们没有这个默认值
  （这正好解释了为什么同事「单请求能跑 700 秒」而你不能）。

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 它是怎么被查出来的：1. 一次非流式探测在 **t = 304.6 s** 死于 `HeadersTimeoutError`——
   这是 **undici 的异常类**，由此暴露了客户端时钟的存在。
2. 回查全部生产失败：静默间隔 **304.6–305.4 s**、`message: "terminated"`、
   全部发生在流中途、且都在内容开始之后。
3. 本地受控复现（本地 SSE 服务器 + 真实 Node fetch）精确复刻指纹：
   最后字节在 `t = 2.045 s` → 报错在 `t = 306.062 s`
   （`TypeError: terminated`，cause `BodyTimeoutError`，code `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT`）；
   而用 `Agent({ bodyTimeout: 0 })` 构造的客户端**挺过 338 秒静默**并把流读完。
   用另一版本 undici 的 `setGlobalDispatcher` 也能修好内置 `fetch`——正是本插件用的注入路径。

仓库自带该复现脚本：

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 它是怎么被查出来的：```bash
node scripts/reproduce-300s.mjs            # 默认 fetch：复现 ~304 秒被杀
node scripts/reproduce-300s.mjs --plugin   # 装上本插件后：挺过 300 秒
```

dsh-stream-timeout-fix README · 开发：```bash
npm install
npm test
```

`npm test` 跑一组快速、确定性的对照：

* **对照**——一个 `bodyTimeout` 极小的 `Agent` 证明静默流会死于
  `UND_ERR_BODY_TIMEOUT`（即线上失败的形状）；
* **修复**——`apply()` 之后同样的静默能读完，且全局 dispatcher 确实是本插件的 agent；
* 外加响应头阶段存活与重复挂载幂等两项检查。
